recipes.name: Crab Dip
ingredients_raw: 2 (6 ounce) cans crabmeat, drained and flaked
1 (1 pound) loaf round, crusty Italian bread

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine crabmeat, cream cheese, mayonnaise, onion, garlic powder, salt, and pepper together in a medium bowl; spread mixture into a 1-quart baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20 minutes. Meanwhile, cut a circle in the top of the bread; scoop out the inside to create a bread bowl. Tear the removed bread into pieces for dipping.
Stir baked crab dip and spoon into bread bowl. Place bread bowl and chunks of bread on a medium baking sheet; bake for an additional 10 minutes. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Crab Dip
raw_recipe.description: This crab dip recipe is easy to make with canned crabmeat, cream cheese, and onion; serve hot in a warm bread bowl for a pleasing party appetizer.

review.reviewBody: I gave this 4 stars instead of 5 because I added a few things to it to make it a little tastier. It was a little bland on it's own. I reduced the cream cheese to 8 oz, and increased the mayo to 3 4ths of a cup. I squirted lemon juice on the crab to eliminate any fishy taste ( i do this to all my seafood). Then I added 2 shakes of cayanne and 3 tablespoons of horseradish. I baked it for 15 minutes, and then topped it with shredded cheddar and monteray jack cheese and baked it until the cheese was lightly golden. With these chages it is a def. 5 star recipe. I think this is a great starter crab dip. Thanks for posting.

What's up, people?? Man, every now and then, I run across recipes on this website that cause me to want to hit somebody because they are so GOOD!!!! Well, this is one of them. I did everything that the recipe called for, but I did add a little sour cream and some sharp chedder cheese in the mixture. I didn't have any Old Bay Seasoning either so I just used a little Tony Chachere's seasoning salt (it's a Louisiana thang, baby). I also sprinkled the top of it with a little more cheese once I put it in the pan. I served it with an Italian loaf that I toasted in the oven for just a little bit to make the bread a little crispy...but don't keep it in too long are the bread will be too hard. Always make sure that you grease the bottom of the pan before you bake it......or just simply spray it with some non-stick cooking spray. Clean-up's a breeze and this dip didn't last long at all. To be honest, I ate it all myself cause I didn't want to share. I'll share the next one, but this was just too darn good.............FOR REAL!!!

I halved this recipe and made several changes per the many suggestions. I sauteed my onions in minced garlic (deleting the need for garlic powder). I added a little lemon juice and around 2-3 tbs of old bay (deleting the salt & pepper). I added about 1 tbs of horseradish and around a 1/2 cup of sour cream. I only used 8 oz of cream cheese and a full pound of fresh crab meat. I also added about a cup of shredded colby jack cheese. The results were amazing. We are from the Chesapeake Bay area and are very picky about our seafood. This was the perfect blend of creamy and spicy. Delicious!

I made this and followed Tiffany"s suggestions. I used 1 pound of Alaskan King Crab, 1/4 cup fresh parsley, 1 Tbs Old Bay, 1 cup of fresh grated Parmesan cheese, sauteed onion, and cooked in stoneware for 20 minutes at 350 and then transferred to a bread bowl and baked for 10 more minutes. Thankful for the recipe and the suggested revisions. I am mainly keeping track of what I did differently to make again because my friends loved it!

I made it as per the recipe (except I had flaked, claw meat not canned). I heated everything together on the stove and served it over noodles instead of as a dip, which worked. It was okay. When I took 2/3 of the mixture and added, 1 stalk chopped celery (pre-sautéed in butter) 1-1/2 C whole milk, 1/2 C heavy cream, 1T Old Bay seasoning, and 1 t Tabasco and made it into soup, it was 10 times better.

This is a great basic recipe to "tweak" up to your own tastes. I used 1 lb. of lump crab meat (fresh), 8 oz neufchatel cheese, 3/4 cup mayo, 1 Tbsp dried minced onion, 1/2 Tbsp Old Bay seasoning, 1 tsp garlic herb seasoning, and also mixed in about 1/2 cup of a shredded Italian 6-cheese mix. I added another 1/2 cup of the cheese mix on top and then baked for 25 minutes in a 1-quart casserole dish. I broiled the top for a few minutes until brown and now my husband says he will never order this in a restaurant again. :)

Great dip for parties! I did tweak the recipe a bit. I used half of a huge, white onion. Also used some Old Bay seasoning and minced garlic (instead of powder). Instead of using crusty Italian bread. I thawed one loaf of frozen bread, formed it to bread bowl size, brushed it with beated egg, and covered it with clear wrap as it rose. Then baked the loaf (at 350 degrees) until golden brown. Cut the top out, insert the dip and some shredded cheese, and then bake until the cheese is melted...YUMMY!

This was a great easily adaptable recipe to serve to friend and family. You might use a 24oz round loaf of bread as i had too much dip for the 16 oz size. I still made it work though! Changes: 8 oz cream cheese, 1/2 cup mayo, 1/4 cup sour cream, 2 tbsp horseradish, 1/8 tsp cayenne. After initial baking, I scooped dip into round and spread the rest in the original baking dish. I sprinkled Monterrey Jack over the rest and after heating i blended cheese into dip. Next time i may use parmesan or a combination. I served with the warm bread, pita chips, and celery sticks. My sister thought it was too crabby but everyone else enjoyed! Thanks!

Followed another reviewer's advice and reduced the cream cheese to 8 ounces and upped the mayo to 3/4th of a cup. Also used a bit more garlic powder and liberal amounts of both black and cayenne pepper since I like lots of kick to my food. Without the additions, I think it would've tasted a bit bland to me. I also didn't use breadbowls, but instead baked this in a 9" cake pan (didn't have any other dishes). Served it with chips cold for an office party and warm while visiting my boyfriend's family. Personally, I liked it cold better, but people enjoyed it both ways!

My Dad is lactose-intolerant and cannot have any dairy. So, I substituted the cream cheese with Vevan Plain Uncream Cheese (Stop and Shop). What a great flavor!!! Can't even tell from the original recipe. So good

Made this for years. Add a good tablespoon of cream of mushroom and a light splash of Worcestershire. Eliminate 1 Tbsp of mayo. Makes all the difference with flavor. Also if you choose, use a package of gelatin to make a wonderful crab mold without the bread.
Great base. Adding in sour cream and old bay.
Fabulous recipe, kids! I followed the directions until taste time, before the oven. Increased garlic by 4X and added Old Bay as well. Wonderful dip.
Simple and delicious!

I added a 1/4 teaspoon of garlic powder and some paprika. I also added crystals hot sauce. It came out perfect. It was a crowd pleaser for sure! There isn’t a lot of bread so be prepared to add some crackers and or tortilla chips.

I just can't get into the taste of canned crab. I make this recipe every time we can get a hold of fresh dungeness crab. If we're lucky, we can get it straight from the boats and cook them ourselves with some Old Bay seasoning. I also sprinkle some paprika on top before baking. It's so delicious!!
Simple and delicious! Worth a try and very easy to make. Didn't do the breadbowl, cooked it fully in a glass pan, but otherwise kept it to the recipe!
Yummy!! Made it for new year's eve and it got gone fast!
I served this Christmas Eve & it was a huge hit! Easy to make.

As written, this is a great basic recipe. Lots of people doctor it up, which is exactly what a great base recipe provides. I added a bit of sour cream, 1/4 cup of shredded cheese, a teaspoon of horseradish, and a tablespoon+ of Old Bay. Oh, and one extra can of crab meat.
